title: What's My IP Address
metaDescription: Find your public IP, ISP, and location instantly. Check if your VPN is leaking your real IP via WebRTC. 100% client-side, nothing logged.
description: See exactly what your IP address reveals about you, and verify your VPN isn't leaking your real IP via WebRTC.

educational.howItWorks: This tool makes two checks when you open the page: (1) it asks our own server what IP address your request arrived from, plus the city/region/country/timezone the edge network already attached to that request — nothing is sent to any third-party IP lookup service; and (2) a WebRTC ICE candidate probe that asks your browser for the IPs it would advertise during a peer-to-peer connection. The WebRTC probe is what reveals VPN leaks — a properly-configured VPN should mask both the server-seen IP AND the WebRTC-advertised IP. If you see your real ISP IP in the WebRTC section while connected to a VPN, the VPN isn't patching WebRTC and sites can still identify you.
tips: Run this tool with your VPN OFF and note your real IP, then turn the VPN ON and run again — both IPs should differ
If WebRTC shows your real IP while the VPN is on, install a WebRTC blocker extension or switch to a VPN that patches the API
ASN and ISP info can fingerprint you across IP changes — using a major VPN provider with a shared exit-IP pool reduces this
Geolocation accuracy is city-level at best — your real location is harder to determine than most people think
Run this tool periodically; some VPN clients lose WebRTC protection after browser updates
commonMistakes: Assuming a VPN is enough — without WebRTC patching, sites can still see your real IP through the browser API
Trusting 'free' VPN providers that may sell your traffic data — your IP is hidden but your activity isn't
Forgetting about IPv6 — many VPNs only tunnel IPv4 and let IPv6 leak through your real ISP
Believing incognito/private browsing hides your IP — it only hides local history, your IP is still visible to every site
Using a browser-only VPN extension while desktop apps (Discord, Steam, etc.) still leak your real IP
